# Plan
Goal: small-business finance system, Python stdlib only. Full spec: .claude/team/spec.md (the user's request; section numbers below refer to it). Read your sections there.
Check (overall): `python -m unittest discover -s tests`. Each task writes tests in tests/test_<task>.py.

## Contract / Conventions (shared code already written & working: fin/core.py, fin/cli.py — read both first, do NOT edit them; if you need a change, log it in changes.md and work around it)
- Each command module `fin/<module>.py` defines `register(reg)` and optionally `SCHEMA` (a string of CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, run on every connect; prefix your table names with your module's own prefix). Call `reg(("txn","add"), setup, handler, access)`; setup(parser) adds argparse args (repeatable options: action="append"); handler(ctx, args) returns the JSON-able result (strings for money via core.fmt). access 'read'|'write'|'admin' — auth is done by cli.py. Write handlers call `ctx.audit(action, target)` once on success. Raise `core.UserError("msg")` for every user error (cli rolls back everything, exit 2). Never use float. Use core.money/fmt/parse_amount/parse_date/parse_month/add_months/month_last_day/next_month, ctx.post_txn (checks closed period, balance, unknown accounts), ctx.ensure_account (auto-created accounts, book currency), ctx.convert, ctx.balances, ctx.require_account. Validate every input (dates, months, decimals, ids) and raise UserError, never a traceback. Don't write your own money/date helpers.
- Handlers must work when called repeatedly in a long-running process (no global state). Don't print; return results.
- Tests: use unittest; run the CLI in-process via `from fin.cli import main` with `--db` in a tempfile dir (capture stdout with contextlib.redirect_stdout / stderr), or via subprocess. Since books isn't done until wave 1 ends, for setup in your tests use main(["--db",db,"init",...]) and then, if `account add`/`txn add` are not yet available, insert via Ctx directly (open `cli.open_db(path)`, `Ctx(conn,'admin')`, `begin`/commit by hand). Keep each test file fast (<20s).
- Module map: fin/books.py (task books), fin/automation.py (automation), fin/billing.py (billing), fin/reports.py + fin/loan.py (reports). Task owns only those files + its tests/test_<task>.py. Don't touch other files. Log any edit to a shared file in .claude/team/changes.md (shouldn't be needed).
- Done check for every task: `python -m unittest tests.test_<task>` (plus your module must import cleanly: `python -m fin --help`).

## books
Spec sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 11 (user add/list, audit list), 12 (period close/status). `init` already exists in cli.py (audit entry 1, user=admin name). Files: fin/books.py, tests/test_books.py. Commands: account add/list, txn add/list, balance, fx add, convert, user add/list, audit list, period close/status. Audit actions/targets as in section 11 (user.add, account.add, txn.add, fx.add, period.close). Note ctx.add_account audits "account.add" itself for the target when exist_ok=False — don't audit twice. `fx add` validates currencies (3 letters, uppercase them) and rate > 0. `--account PREFIX` in txn list matches the account or its descendants. `period close` earlier than already-closed changes nothing (and no audit entry — assumption). `balance` includes ancestors summed over descendants; sort keys by account, currencies sorted. convert output: amount rounded to cents.

## automation
Spec sections 5 (rule add/list, import), 6 (budget set, report budget), 7 (recurring add/run). Files: fin/automation.py, tests/test_automation.py. Import: use the csv module; the whole import is one transaction (cli rolls back on any error, so closed-period rows or bad rows fail everything); category accounts created via ctx.ensure_account; ACCOUNT must exist; duplicates tracked in your own table (SCHEMA, prefix `imp_`) keyed by (account,date,desc,amount) — count repeats within the file as skipped. Rule account must exist at `rule add` (assumption) and pattern must be a valid regex. Import row posting: ACCOUNT gets the row amount, category gets the opposite; an amount of 0 is a user error. Budget: account must be an existing expense account (or descendant of Expenses). Recurring: store the postings (validate at add by a dry check: balance, accounts exist — don't create a txn), track created occurrence dates in your own table; `recurring run` posts through ctx.post_txn; audit recurring.add (name) and recurring.run (the --until date); recurring name unique.

## billing
Spec sections 13, 14, 15 (tax add/list, customer/vendor add/list, invoice create/issue/pay/show/list, bill create/pay/show/list, report aging incl. --payables, report tax). Files: fin/billing.py, tests/test_billing.py. Tables in SCHEMA with prefix `bil_`. Audit actions as in section 11 (tax.add, customer.add, vendor.add, invoice.create/issue/pay, bill.create/pay with the id as string). Tax rate is stored and shown as given (string). Aging for payables mirrors receivables (bills dated <= DATE, payments dated <= DATE). `invoice pay`/`bill pay`: check closed period on the payment date (ctx.post_txn does it); ACCOUNT of invoice pay must be an asset account; bill pay ACCOUNT must be an asset account too (assumption). Invoice `issue` checks closed period of the invoice date. Invoice list --status filters draft/issued/partial/paid. Amounts: positive quantity/price required? Allow any decimal but quantity must be > 0 (assumption). Report tax `by_code` includes codes used by issued invoices and bills in the period; amounts per code are tax sums. Bill status open/partial/paid. Invoice `due` = date + terms days.

## reports
Spec sections 8 (report income, balance-sheet, networth), 9 (loan schedule), 16 (reconcile), 17 (trial-balance, ledger). Files: fin/reports.py, fin/loan.py (register in both; loan.py only loan schedule), tests/test_reports.py. Reconcile table in SCHEMA prefix `rec_`. Conversion: per (account,currency) balance converted with ctx.convert at the report date, rounded with money() per account entry (accounts appear by name the postings are on, summed across currencies after conversion). Net/totals: sum of rounded entries. Reports with no --currency use the book currency (still convert other-currency postings). Income report: income positive = -raw; expenses = raw. Balance sheet: assets raw, liabilities/equity negated; retained_earnings = -(sum of income+expense raw), total_equity = equity + retained_earnings. Networth month entries: all months from..to inclusive, book currency. Ledger: ACCOUNT must exist, amounts in the account's currency (postings to descendants with other currencies: convert at the posting date? assumption: convert at the --to date). Trial balance rows by exact account name sorted. Reconcile: audit action `reconcile` target ACCOUNT; ACCOUNT must exist; `--clear` ids must be integers with a posting to ACCOUNT dated <= DATE; no-op marks for already-cleared are fine. Loan: per spec; validate principal>0, months>=1, rate>=0. Use Decimal with enough precision (getcontext().prec = 50 locally via decimal.localcontext).

## api (wave 2)
Spec section 10 + the API parts of 11. File: fin/api.py (`serve(db, port)` blocking, ThreadingHTTPServer; wire `serve --port N` into cli via fin/api.py `register(reg)` — add "api" to cli.MODULES is NOT allowed to you, the lead already adds it), tests/test_api.py. Implement every route by translating to `fin.cli.execute(db, user, argv)` (GET: user from X-User if given, else None; POST: X-User required). Map AuthError .status to 401/403, other UserError to 400 with {"error": msg}, unknown path 404, invalid JSON body 400. POST /transactions body → `txn add` argv (posting without amount → just ACCOUNT). Invoices: `invoice create --line "desc;qty;price;tax"`, issue, pay (`invoice pay ID AMOUNT --date --account`). Reports: income (from,to), balance-sheet (at), aging (at, payables=1). `/audit` → audit list. GET /balances?at= optional. Tests start the server on port 0/free port in a thread and use urllib.
